At	least	five	events	topped	the	economic	loss	threshold	of	
$10	billion.	Hurricane	Ian	dominated	the	ranking	with	an	
aggregated	toll	of	approximately	$95.5	billion	—	more	than	
the	next	seven	events	combined.	Three	drought	events	in	the	
table	of	10	costliest	events	underline	the	growing	significance	
of	the	peril	on	a	global	scale.	Particularly ,	cumulative	drought	
losses	in	European	countries	were	at	their	highest	since	 
the	historic	summer	of	2003,	while	the	U.S.	had	the	worst	
drought	since	2012	in	terms	of	overall	economic	losses.	
Floods	in	Pakistan	were	the	costliest	event	for	the	peril,	 
tied	with	seasonal	flood	losses	in	China,	which	were	at	
their	lowest	since	2015.	All	but	one	event	in	the	table	were	
weather-	and	climate-related;	the	only	two	geophysical	
disasters	that	topped	$1	billion	in	economic	losses	in	 
2022	were	the	March	Fukushima	Earthquake	in	Japan	 
and	September	Sichuan	Earthquake	in	China.
